requirements.summary: Repositories must expose compact maps, mechanical invariants, and filesystem surfaces that agents can navigate without relying on author memory.
Local worktree-scoped logs, metrics, traces, runtime state, and failure evidence must be queryable by agents and used in repair loops.

sources.title: Build iterative repair loops with Codex

requirements.summary: Validation feedback must become structured repair input in a review, repair, validate loop rather than dead-end logs or manual spelunking.
Workflow runs must expose traceable model, tool, guardrail, and custom spans that can be inspected before outputs influence claims.
Runs must have coherent traces with root spans, child spans, processors/exporters, and enough metadata to debug and evaluate workflows.
Monitoring must support alerting, investigation, diagnosis, visualization, before/after comparison, trend understanding, and freshness-sensitive interpretation.
Latency, traffic, errors, and saturation must be translated into command, check, fixture, receipt, query, cache, process, and exporter measurements.

sources.title: Live Your Best Life With Structured Events

requirements.summary: Events should be wide and richly structured so agents can ask new questions and localize unknown failures without dashboard theater.
Run, correlation, trace, receipt, candidate, law, check, and claim identifiers are essential correlation keys, while metrics labels must remain bounded and redacted.
Logs, metrics, traces, and resources need consistent semantic names and attributes so telemetry can correlate across signals.
Agent improvement must connect traces and feedback to generated evals, ranked repairs, validation, before/after comparison, and durable promotion.
Domain-agent improvement claims require realistic domain tasks, expert-source feedback, rubrics, error taxonomy, eval generation, ranked repair, and before/after proof.

sources.title: Attached Rust Developer Experience Governance Proposal

requirements.summary: Cargo and Rust tools are observations; only ultragoal may convert tool output into typed same-candidate receipts and claim ceilings.
TypeScript and UI repos require pinned toolchains, strict type/lint/test/browser/accessibility coverage, governed parsers, and CLI receipts before tool output can affect claims.
